We've criss-crossed Japan as well as visiting South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia (Penang), Indonesia (Bali), the Philippines, and Thailand. Mid-sized towns are usually our favorite -- they're easy to get around in, and are (generally) more relaxing than some of the bigger cities. We unfortunately aren't considering China or India due to air pollution fears, but are willing to consider any other Asian city famed for its food.

As an example, I was all-in on visiting Hoi An until I learned it would probably be flooded during my vacation time. If you know of any similar cities with great atmosphere and great food, please share! Thanks for the recommendations. :D

I can only recommend Laos to you! It's a beatiful country with wonderful people, delicious food and really cheap.

Cambodia had some of the more interesting food we've eaten. It was adventurous but still accessible, like a soup with a half formed duck embryo. We didn't get out of Siam Reap, but there were plenty of places to try as well as a night market with stands where you ate on a blanket set on the ground. The food can be hit or miss, but it will be interesting if nothing else. Food tours are available in Siam Reap, and I recommend them.

Myanmar is only up for consideration if you love fish sauce. Like you order eggplant but really want it to taste like fish sauce. And you want your rice to taste like fish sauce, so there's fish paste just for that. And that you didn't want chicken, you really wanted fish with chicken texture.

She used to cut and hit me when demanding that I tell her that I love her.

When people tell me that they love me, I can't help but feel bile rising up my throat, and the cold chill of fear working their ways through my veins, screaming for me to run. To hide, to find shelter, to get away from danger. When people touch me, I flinch away as if they've just run the blade of a knife along my skin. When people look at me, I stare back with fire burning in my eyes, they always look away first.

I stand against those fears. I smile and tell them that I love them too. I hug them. I remember to not let them to see my scarred soul.

I wonder what kind of man I would be today without my scars. Was I tempered like steel, or was I crippled by her?
